title: Measuring the Sr$^+$ 5s$_{1/2}$ Landé $g$-factor Using Singlet-Triplet Oscillations in a Circular Rydberg State of Strontium
authors: Baptiste Muraz, Mathis Pepin, Corentin Guimard, Michel Brune, Brice Bakkali-Hassani, Sébastien Gleyzes
abstract: Circular states of strontium are promising platforms for quantum technologies. They exhibit much longer lifetimes than laser-accessible Rydberg states and possess an optically active ionic core that can be manipulated with laser light. Here we trap circular states in optical tweezers by exploiting the dynamical polarizability of the ionic core. We measure the decay of the orbital component of a n=51 circular state and observe singlet-triplet spin oscillations arising from the interplay of vector light shifts induced by the optical tweezers, spin-orbit coupling associated with the Rydberg electron, and the difference in Landé $g$-factor between the ionic core and the Rydberg electrons. By observing the two electron spin dynamics, we measure the spin-orbit interaction and the correction $δg \sim$ 10^(-5) of the Landé $g$-factor of the Sr$^+$ 5s$_{1/2}$ ionic core electron with respect to that of a free electron. This provides a first high-precision measurement of $g_{\textrm{Sr}^+, 5s_{1/2}}$ = 2.002290(1).
summary: The researchers measured the Landé g-factor of the $	ext{Sr}^+$ $5s_{1/2}$ core electron by studying singlet-triplet spin oscillations in circular Rydberg states. They trapped these states using optical tweezers and observed the spin dynamics by monitoring population decay. This provided a first high-precision determination of the core's g-factor, advancing quantum metrology using alkaline-earth atoms.
main_problem: To precisely measure the Landé g-factor of the Sr$^+$ $5s_{1/2}$ ionic core electron.
main_result: The measurement yields a high-precision value for the Landé g-factor: $g_{	ext{Sr}^+, 5s_{1/2}} = 2.002290(1)$.
method: The measurement relies on observing and analyzing singlet-triplet spin oscillations in a circular Rydberg state of Strontium, which are sensitive to the difference in Landé g-factors.
model_or_system: The system uses circular Rydberg states of $	ext{Sr}^+$ trapped in optical tweezers. The physics is modeled by considering the interplay between spin-orbit coupling, vector light shifts from the tweezers, and the difference in Landé g-factors between the core and Rydberg electrons.
key_observables: Damped oscillations of the recapture signal (singlet-triplet dynamics) as a function of time delay, and the oscillation frequency dependence on the external magnetic field $B_0$.
important_parameters: The measured difference in Landé g-factor ($\delta g \sim 10^{-5}$), the lifetime of the $51c$ state ($1.8(1)\ 	ext{ms}$), and the external magnetic field $B_0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the spin dynamics are governed by the effective spin Hamiltonian derived from the interaction of the two electron spins with the magnetic field, and that the observed oscillations are dominated by the $\delta g$ term.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup (trapping, detection), the time evolution of circular state populations, and the measured spin oscillations as a function of time delay and external magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup for trapping and preparing circular Rydberg states, describes the optical detection scheme to isolate singlet atoms, and finally presents the measurement of spin-orbit coupling and the Landé g-factor by fitting the magnetic field dependence of the spin oscillation frequency.
why_interesting: This work provides a high-precision quantum measurement of an atomic property ($g$-factor) using highly excited, long-lived Rydberg states, demonstrating advanced control over complex multi-electron spin dynamics in an optical tweezer platform.
